title: Interviews under Compulsion
summary: How to plan and conduct compelled interviews with firm staff and subjects, balancing effective questioning with the rights of the interviewee.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to plan and conduct compelled interviews with firm staff and subjects, balancing effective questioning with the rights of the interviewee.
Learning Objectives: Plan a compelled interview strategy and question outline
Conduct interviews that are fair, structured and evidentially sound
Handle legal representatives, privilege objections and evasive answers
Syllabus: Compelled and voluntary interviews: rights, cautions and use of answers
Interview planning, document bundles and questioning structure
Managing lawyers, objections and difficult interviewees
Role-play: interviewing a senior manager under compulsion
Intended Audience: Enforcement investigators, case managers and lawyers
Supervisory staff seconded to or working alongside enforcement teams
Staff moving into enforcement from supervision, authorisation or other agencies
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of enforcement, supervision or legal casework is helpful. No prior investigative training is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2015), Credible Deterrence in the Enforcement of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2016), Enhanced Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding Concerning Consultation and Cooperation and the Exchange of Information
